LEISUREWORLD TERMS AND CONDITIONS 
LEISUREWORLD TERMS AND CONDITIONS | 
This document is subject to change. Please be aware the copy you hold may be out of date. The 
latest version is available directly from your club. 
10/07/2026 
 
 
ADMISSION POLICY 
 
 
 Admission to the leisure centre is subject to the centres admission fees either membership or 
pay as you go charges 
 Facility users must scan their barcode or check in at reception to record their attendance and 
gain access to the various areas and activities with the centre 
 Admission to the leisure centre is based on a current timetable which is subject to change 
 Admission to Sauna/Steam room is strictly for over 18’s only 
 Adult gym sessions are for over 18’s only 
 Student gym and swim sessions are for over 16’s only 
 Teen gym and swim sessions are for ages 13-15 years only 
 All teens must complete a gym safety induction prior to accessing the gym or fitness classes. 
 All gym patrons must sign a Health Declaration at sign up 
 If you know or are concerned you have a medical condition which might interfere with 
exercising safely you should get advice from the relevant medical professional and follow any 
advice given before using the facility. 
 Our pools have max bather loads for the safety of all patrons. Please note if these are reached, 
access may be restricted until safe levels return. 
 People under the influence of alcohol or drugs will be refused entry to the leisure centre 
 During Swimming Lessons a parent is requested to stay on site. 
 
 
 
CHILDRENS ADMISSION 
• Children aged under 8 years must be accompanied by a responsible adult (18 years or over) in 
the water in the ratio max 2 children to 1 adult 
o Supervision from the viewing gallery or pool deck will not be accepted as adequate 
supervision. 
• Children 8yrs – 10yrs must have an Adult (over 18yrs) in the building 
• Children must be supervised by an adult at all times while in the centre. 
• Supervising adults must comply with safe supervision ratios of parent/guardian to child while 
in the pool 
 
Please follow the rules and advise on display for the various activities at the centre. These rules and 
information are in order to ensure that everyone may continue to enjoy a safe and pleasant facility. 
 
Any person(s) that do not abide by the rules set out by the Management may be asked to leave

On joining, the facility user automatically accepts and agrees to be bound by these conditions. Pay 
As You Go users automatically accept and agrees to be bound by these conditions or by virtue of 
using our services. 
 
ACCESS 
All visitors must register with LeisureWorld to use our services. Children must be registered by their 
parent or guardian. All visitors must record their attendance. 
 
Each facility user can generate a barcode in the LeisureWorld app to gain entry. All facility user must 
record a visit by swiping or checking in at reception, no exceptions. 
 
MEMBERSHIP CANCELLATION POLICIES 
There is a 28-day notification period of your intention to cancel a monthly membership. Cancellation 
via phone call is not accepted. 
 
Members must contact via email to cancellations@leisureworldcork.com. Cancelling a direct debit 
with your bank is not valid notice as we are not informed of these cancellations. 
 
If you purchase your membership online, you have 14 days to change your mind before you use your 
membership. Cooling off is only applicable to change of mind and non -use. LeisureWorld will waive 
the exclusion for services that have already started, i.e., y ou selected your membership to start 
immediately but did not use it. 
 
Our terms and conditions will come into force automatically after the 14-day period has 
elapsed. In person purchases of goods and services are not entitled to a cooling off period. 
 
For information   about your consumer rights relating to contracts please refer to 
https://www.ccpc.ie/consumers/contracts-and-services/gym-contracts 
 
MEMBERSHIP FREEZE OPTION 
You can freeze your membership for a minimum of one month’s up to a maximum of 3 months. You 
can do this once per calendar year. Monthly members can only freeze for whole months. Freezing of 
your membership can only be granted with a prior written request from the member/user and 
approval from the management. 
 
Periods of non-use of the facilities cannot be backdated under any circumstances. Couple members 
are not able to be frozen individually, both memberships must be frozen together. 
 
MONTHLY BILLING 
Membership payments are due regardless of usage. New members agree to a minimum commitment 
of one full billing cycle, that is one payment must be collected before you can terminate. This contract 
automatically renews after the minimum period of 1 month and will continue indefinitely unless 
cancelled by the member. We require 28 days notification via email to 
cancellations@leisureworldcork.com of your intention to cancel a monthly membership. 
 
Please note we cannot part bill a month if your next billing date falls within your notice period you will 
be billed for the next full month and your membership will finish at the end of that monthly cycle. 
Monthly membership billing is done via direct debit.

TERMINATION OF MEMBERSHIP 
Management reserve the right to terminate any membership for violation of any rules or regulations 
of the facility, or for conduct deemed by the management to be detrimental to the safety and welfare, 
good order, or character of the facility, it’s staff or its members and facility users. 
 
TRANSFER OF MEMBERSHIP 
Memberships may not be transferred or assigned to another person. Membership deposits and fees 
are not refundable under any circumstances. The registered member/facilityuser is the only person 
that can use the membership, no sharing is permitted. 
 
REFUND POLICY 
A refund for non-use of membership will not be granted under any circumstances. 
 
Courses and fitness class bookings are paid in full and non-refundable. If a class is cancelled in advance 
by the facility user, in line with the cancellation policy, a booking credit note will be issued to your 
membership account. 
 
Courses and fitness class bookings are paid in full and non -refundable. If a class is cancelled by the 
facility, a credit note will be issued be issue to your account or a request can be made for a refund. 
 
Any request for refund should be made prior to your service booking commencing. Once a service 
booking has started requests for refunds will be rejected. 
 
In circumstances where a customer has been advised that they cannot make use of 
membership/class/course by a medical professional, we can review a request for a credit for time 
missed due to illness or injury if it is accompanied by an appropriate dated medical note. Any request 
for a medical refund must be made to the facility via email to info@leisureworldcork.com. 
 
RETURNS POLICY 
Any product bought at LeisureWorld that is faulty should be returned accompanied with a receipt as 
proof of purchase. This should be done at the site the product was purchased at. Products that have 
been purchased and are broken by use, and not due to defects, are not eligible for a refund.

GENERAL CODE OF CONDUCT 
 
Safe Selling & Use of Supplements  
Any supplements or sports foods sold or permitted within the facility adhere strictly to our Safe Selling 
Supplements and Sport Food Statement. Members and users are advised to consume sports nutrition 
responsibly and in accordance with manufacturer guidelines and professional dietary advice. 
 
MOBILE PHONES, CAMERAS, AND RECORDING EQUIPMENT 
Mobile phones are prohibited for use in the changing rooms and swimming pool areas. Please respect 
other facility users right to privacy and to work out without being recorded or photographed. You are 
not permitted to take photos or record videos that contain personal data of others, especially if you 
intend to share your recordings with others. Recording or photographing facility users  without their 
permission may result in termination of membership. 
 
LOCKERS 
Lockers must be used by all facility users to secure belongings. Lockers operate using a €1 coin or 
token to secure the locker, and it is returned when the locker is opened. The  facility user 
acknowledges that the facility will not be responsible for the loss of any personal items or damage 
to personal property, either on the facility or in the facility car parking areas. LeisureWorld accepts 
no responsibility for personal items that are brought into the facility by facility users. LeisureWorld 
will not accept custody of personal items, you must use the lockers provided. 
 
FACILTY CONDITION 
The facility management will use its best endeavours to ensure that all facilities, apparatus, and 
equipment are maintained in working order but accepts no responsibility to the facility user for failure 
or breakdown of any equipment or apparatus however caused. You must inform staff of any defect 
you notice or become aware of while using the facility, to allow our staff make good and safe any 
defects. 
 
DISPUTES 
In the event of any dispute arising between a facility user of the facility and the management of the 
facility, the decision of LeisureWorld management will be final. 
 
FITNESS CLASSES 
Classes are available for persons aged over 16 years only unless otherwise stated. 60 minutes notice is 
required to cancel a class booking. You must scan your access card or check in at reception to register 
attendance, no exceptions. 
 
SWIMMING POOL USE 
All users of the swimming pool must use the showers before entering the pool. Swim caps must be 
worn. No outdoor footwear is permitted on the pool deck. Swimmers are encouraged to wear 
appropriate footwear on the pool deck and in the changing areas. A full list of rules and regulations 
are in place in each of the pool areas, facility users must agree to comply with the regulations in each 
area.

MEMBERSHIP TYPES 
 
Pay As You Go Membership 
PAYG membership is available for all adults, students and children to access our services on an ad-hoc 
basis. Payment is made for each visit by way of access tickets or bookings. Itis free to register as a Pay 
As You Go member. 
 
Adult Membership 
To qualify for this membership, you must be aged between 18 years and older This membership allows 
one person to use our service. Adult membership is available for either all services or for swim only. 
 
Over 65 Membership 
To qualify for this membership, you must be aged 65 year or older This membership allows one person 
to use our service. ID is required when enrolling for this membership. 
 
Unemployed Membership 
To qualify for this membership, you must provide proof of unemployment. This membership allows 
one person to use our service. ID is required when enrolling for this membership. 
 
Couple Membership 
This gives a family the opportunity to jointly purchase memberships. There will be a primary and a linked 
member. Payments are assigned to the primary member. Each facility user will receive an individual 
membership card. If the primary facility user fails to make the monthly payment, both memberships will 
be withdrawn. All changes to the membership must be made by the primary facility user. 
 
Student Membership 
To qualify for student membership, you must be aged 16 or over, or be enrolled in full-time education 
programmes if over 18 years old. Part-time and professional education programmes are not valid for 
student memberships. If under 18 we require photo ID. Production of a valid student ID with expiry 
date on the card or dated proof of enrolment is required to purchase these memberships if you are 
over 18 years old. 
 
Child Pool membership 
To qualify for child membership, you must be aged 6 -17. Child memberships are only available when 
linked to an adult membership. Use of a child membership must comply with Admission policy. 
 
Teen membership 
To qualify for teen membership, you must be aged 13-17. Teen memberships permit access to the pool, 
gym and fitness classes. Teen members are required to complete a safety induction with a trainer prior 
to using the gym. 
 
 
PRIVACY POLICY 
 
A copy of our privacy is available online at https://www.leisureworldcork.com/privacy-policy/

label: LeisureWorld Admission Policy
text:
Leisureworld Admission Policy 
 
General Admission 
● Admission to the Leisure Centre is subject to the applicable admission fees, either through membership or pay- 
as-you-go charges. 
 
● Members must scan their barcode or check in at reception to record their attendance and gain access to the 
facilities. 
 
● Access is based on the current timetable of activities, which is subject to change. 
 
● Admission to the Sauna and Steam Room is strictly restricted to persons aged 18 years and over. 
 
● Adult gym sessions are open to 18 years and over. 
 
● Student gym and swim sessions are open to those aged 16 years and over. 
 
● Teen gym and swim sessions are available to those aged 13–15 years. 
 
● All teens must complete a gym safety induction prior to using the gym or attending fitness classes. 
 
● All gym patrons must complete and sign a Health Declaration upon registration. 
 
● If you have, or suspect you may have, a medical condition that could interfere with safe exercise, you must seek 
advice from a relevant medical professional and follow that guidance before using any facility. 
 
● Pool use is subject to maximum bather loads for safety reasons. If capacity is reached, admission may be 
temporarily restricted. 
 
● Entry will be refused to anyone under the influence of alcohol or drugs. 
 
● During swimming lessons a parent/guardian is required to remain on site for the duration of the lesson. 
 
 
Children’s Admission 
● Children under 10 years must be accompanied in the water by a responsible adult (18+), at a ratio of 1 adult to 
a maximum of 2 children. 
- Supervision from the viewing gallery or poolside is not considered adequate supervision. 
 
● Children aged 10–12 years must have a responsible adult (18+) present within the building. 
 
● Children must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times while in the centre. 
 
● Supervising adults must adhere to the required safe supervision ratios while children are in the pool. 
 
 
Conduct and Compliance 
● All users must comply with the rules and guidelines displayed throughout the centre. 
 
● These rules are in place to ensure that all visitors can enjoy a safe, welcoming, and pleasant environment. 
 
● Any person who does not comply with this policy or who disregards the instructions of Management may be 
refused entry or asked to leave the premises. 
 
Effective Date: 20 August 2025

Reviewed June 29 2026                                                                                         OPS-POL-05 LeisureWorld Child Admission Policy V1 
 
 
 
Child Admission Policy 
 
 
Purpose 
The purpose of this policy is to ensure the safety, wellbeing, and effective supervision of all children utilising the 
leisure facilities, including the swimming pool, gym, and organised camps. It provides a framework for parents,  
guardians, and staff to maintain a secure environment in compliance with national safety standards. 
 
Scope 
This policy applies to all minors (under 18 years of age), their parents/guardians, and staff members within the 
LeisureWorld facility. It covers general public admissions, swimming lessons, and specialised kids' camps. 
 
Principles 
• Safety First: The safety of the child is the paramount consideration in all 
• activities. 
• Parental Responsibility: Parents or guardians maintain primary responsibility for their children unless the 
child is signed into a programmed activity. 
• Inclusion: Services are provided consistently and transparently, regardless of disability or other protected 
characteristics. 
• Compliance: All users must adhere to LeisureWorld rules and staff instructions to maintain a pleasant 
environment. 
 
Supervision and Access 
LeisureWorld operates strictly enforced supervision ratios to ensure the safety of all minors. These ratios are based 
on national safety guidelines and vary by activity. 
• All specific age-related access rules and supervision ratios are outlined in the Appendix: Access and 
Supervision Requirements 
• Supervision ratios are determined by industry safety standards, risk assessments, and insurance 
requirements. 
• Management reserves the right to amend these ratios based on safety assessments. Parents are 
responsible for reviewing these requirements prior to their visit. 
 
General Requirements 
• Health Declarations: All children participating in activities and gym patrons must have a completed screening 
or health declaration form on file. 
• Medical Conditions: Parents must disclose any medical conditions (e.g., Asthma, Epilepsy, Diabetes) or 
additional needs to ensure staff can provide necessary accommodations. 
• Induction: All teens must complete a gym safety induction prior to using the gym or attending fitness classes. 
• Code of Conduct: LeisureWorld maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding the use or possession of drugs, 
alcohol, or aggressive/anti-social behavior. Any individual found in breach of this code will be refused entry 
or removed from the premises immediately. 
• Exclusions: Management reserves the right to exclude individuals for behavioural issues or non-compliance 
with safety rules. 
 
Review 
This policy will be reviewed annually, or earlier if required

Groups must provide a manifest of all participants and adhere to the following: 
• Dry-Side Activities: 2 : 25 (Leader to Child).

label: LeisureWorld Disability Inclusion Policy
text:
Reviewed June 29 2026 OPS-POL-05 LeisureWorld Child Admission Policy V1 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Disability Inclusion Policy 
 
 
The mission of LeisureWorld is to value the abilities and individuality of people with disabilities by providing 
opportunities for them to reach their full potential within an inclusive culture. At LeisureWorld, we will achieve 
disability inclusion by: 
 
• Continuously reviewing our approach, which involves members, staff, and management.  
• Partnering with clubs, disability services, and consulting with people with disabilities and their  families. 
 
This ensures that our organisation is inclusive for everyone. We welcome all community members, regardless of 
their abilities, and strive to include people with disabilities in both playing and non- playing roles as fully as possible. 
 
 
Our Commitments: 
 
• Legislation Compliance: We are committed to complying with the Equal Status Acts 2000-2012, the 
Disability Act 2005, and Article 30.5 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with 
Disabilities. 
• Sports Inclusion: We fulfill the requirements of the Sports Ireland Policy on Participation in Sport by People 
with Disabilities and engage with the Sport Inclusion Disability Charter. 
• Accessibility: We aim to make our environment, clubs, training, and facilities accessible to people 
with disabilities. We consider reasonable adjustments to achieve this goal effectively. 
 
Facilities and Services: 
 
• Parking: We have disability parking spaces directly outside LeisureWorld entrance. 
• Pool: Our pool has steps leading into the shallow end or we have use of a hoist. 
• Changing Rooms: Accessible changing rooms with showers and toilets are available. These are easily 
accessible from the pool changing area and provide direct access to the pool. 
• Staff Assistance: Our trained staff, including lifeguards, are available to assist with entering and exiting 
the water. 
• Gym Access: The gym is accessible via lifts. It features wide spaces and brightly colour contrasted 
equipment. Wheelchair-accessible equipment includes: 
o Dual Adjustable Pulley: For various strength training exercises. 
o Ski Erg: For cardio and strength work with adjustable resistance. 
o Assault Bike: Usable with arms only, legs only, or both for cardio. 
o Free Weights: Suitable for standing or sitting exercises. 
o Upper arm Ergometer: For cardio with removable seat for wheelchair access. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Reviewed June 29 2026 OPS-POL-05 LeisureWorld Child Admission Policy V1 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Our Goals: 
 
By enhancing our capacity and capabilities, we strive to deliver inclusive programs, advocate for disability inclusion, 
and increase participation by people with disabilities in our sports and organisation.  
 
Our Actions: 
 
• Inclusive Approach: We will adopt an inclusive approach across all aspects of the organisation by 
consulting with our members. 
• Consultation: We will listen to the voices of people with disabilities in all our deliberations and 
program development. 
• Partnerships: We will work with other organisations and advocates for disability inclusion.  
• Governance: We will promote good governance to ensure the participation of people with disabilities.  
• Recognition: We will acknowledge and support the contributions, achievements, and successes of people 
with disabilities in our organisation. 
• Commitment: We commit to adopting the Sport Inclusion Disability Charter. 
 
We will review our Disability Inclusion Policy annually to meet the requirements of each individual and provide them 
with the opportunities they need to reach their full potential.

label: LeisureWorld Community Engagement & Public Relations Policy
text:
Reviewed June 29 2026                                                                 LeisureWorld Community Engagement & Public Relations Policy V1 
 
 
 
Community Engagement & 
Public Relations Policy 
 
 
At LeisureWorld, our policy to interact with our local community and surrounding areas is vital. We are committed t o 
fostering strong community relationships and promoting health and fitness among all age groups. Our initiatives are 
designed to make fitness accessible, engaging, and supportive for everyone in our community.  
 
Community Engagement Inititives 
 
Partnerships with Local Groups 
• We have established partnerships with groups, such as Down Syndrome Cork & Headway, offering 
them discounted rates to encourage participation. 
• We are continually engaging with new groups to expand our outreach and support the local community.  
• We partner with the HSE on numerous programmes, such as the Functional Zone (NPTP), MoveWell 
and more. 
 
Youth Engagement 
• Recognising the importance of youth in the fitness sector, we offer special rates to teens.  
• Teens receive a comprehensive safety gym assessment and a personalised program from one of our qualified 
instructors, ensuring they are educated on the proper use of gym equipment. 
 
Swimming Programs 
• We offer swimming lessons for both children and adults in the community, regardless of membership status.  
• We work with Swim Ireland to organise the “Swim a for a Mile" challenge which has supported local 
charities. 
• We partnered with Cork Sports Partnership to launch Swimming Women, a programme specifically for midlife 
females to support them through life’s milestones. 
 
Programs for the Older Adults 
• We run a weekly Aquafit Class for the active Older adult community. 
• We run fitness classes for older adults to help increase their overall fitness and wellbeing, such as  
Movewell 
 
Community Events and Support 
• We hold an annual event for National Fitness Day, open to the public, to promote health and fitness. 
• LeisureWorld supports local functions by offering spot prises of gym memberships & Family Swims.  
• We sponsor the local basketball club, Neptune Basketball Team. 
Review 
 
This policy will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains relevant and effective in achieving its objectives. Updates will 
be made as necessary to adapt to changing community needs and organisational goals. By adhering to this Community 
Engagement and Public Relations Policy, LeisureWorld aims to foster a supportive and vibrant community, enhance its 
reputation, and ensure transparent and effective communication with all stakeholders.

Reviewed June 29 2026 OPS-POL-05 LeisureWorld Child Admission Policy V1 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Environmental Policy 
 
 
 
 
This policy statement provides the framework on which our environmental programme is based. 
 
We are committed to providing a quality service in a manner that ensures a safe and healthy 
workplace for our employees and minimizes our potential impact on the environment. 
 
We continuously strive to mitigate any harmful effects of our activities on the environment. 
 
We will operate in compliance with all relevant environmental legislation and we will strive to use 
pollution prevention and environmental best practices in all we do. 
 
We will:- 
 
 
• Integrate the consideration of environmental concerns and impacts into all of our decision 
making and activities 
• Minimise waste by evaluating operations and ensuring they are as efficient as possible. 
• We will seek opportunities to reduce our water and energy consumption when possible 
• Meet or exceed all the environmental legislation that relates to the Company. 
• Actively promote environmental awareness and recycling among our employees and 
suppliers 
• Avoid unnecessary use of hazardous materials and products, seek substitutions when 
feasible, and take all reasonable steps to protect human health and the environment when 
such materials must be used and stored 
• Communicate our environmental commitment to clients, customers and the public and 
encourage them to support it 
 
 
To ensure continuous progress toward our sustainability goals, this Environmental Policy will be 
reviewed and updated annually.

label: Child Safeguarding Statement
text:
Child Safeguarding Statement 
 
 
“We at LeisureWorld want to make sure that our children are protected and kept safe from harm while 
they are in the care of the staff and volunteers in LeisureWorld”. 
We do this by: 
 
Giving parents, children and employees information about what we do and what you expect from us Making 
sure that our staﬀ and volunteers are carefully selected, Gardaí Vetted, trained and supervised  
Letting parents and children know how to voice their concerns or complain if there is anything they are not happy 
about. 
 
At LeisureWorld we provide two Designated Liaison Persons. 
 
The primary role of the Designated Liaison Person is to be available to any child or parent who has concerns under the 
“Code of Ethic” and under the Swim Ireland Child Protection Complaints Law.  
On receipt of a complaint the Designated Liaison Person in contact with their counterparts meet and assess concerns with 
reference to the “Code of Ethic’ and Code of Behaviour between workers and children.  
The Designated Liaison Person may seek advice from Swim Ireland protection oﬃcers and if necessary from either the 
local Social Service or organisations such as the ISPCC. 
The Designated Liaison Person and LeisureWorld have no role in investigating child abuse complaints but the CEO must 
be informed of the involvement of statutory authorities in strict conﬁdence.  
 
Concerns about possible unsafe practice may be dealt with by LeisureWorld but the Designated Liaison Person must not 
give details that would indicate their sources unless the complainant has so indicated to the Designated Liaison Person. 
 
The Designated Liaison Person for LeisureWorld Churchfield are Fernando Serina, Justin Theunissen & 
Jason Sheahan and can be contacted at dlp@leisureworldcork.com 
 
Thank you, 
 
Fernando Serina, Senior Manager

label: LeisureWorld Clean Sport & Anti-Doping Policy
text:
Reviewed June 29 2026 Clean Sport & Anti – Doping Policy V1 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Clean Sport & Anti-Doping Policy 
 
Commitment to Clean Sport 
LeisureWorld is committed to protecting the health of our customers, the integrity of our community, and the 
spirit of fair play. The facility operates a strict zero-tolerance policy toward the use, possession, or 
distribution of Performance Enhancing Drugs (PEDs) and prohibited substances, applying equally to 
competitive athletes and recreational customers. 
 
Regulatory Alignment 
This policy is aligned with the standards and frameworks established by Sport Ireland, Ireland Active, the 
World Health Organization (WHO), and the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA). 
 
Customer Obligations & Strict Liability 
By using LeisureWorld facilities, you expressly agree to the following conditions: 
 
● Compliance with WADA Code: Customers must not use, possess, traffic, or attempt to distribute any 
substances or methods featured on the current WADA Prohibited List (2026), including but not limited to 
anabolic agents, hormones, and stimulants. 
 
● Strict Liability: In accordance with international anti-doping principles, the rule of "Strict Liability" 
applies. Customers are solely and personally responsible for any substances found within their body, 
equipment, or personal property while on LeisureWorld premises. 
 
● Supplement and Medication Awareness: It is the sole responsibility of the customer to verify that any 
medications or nutritional supplements they consume are safe and permitted.  
○ LeisureWorld strongly advises members to check medications via the Medcheck tool on 
SportIreland.ie (or Eirpharm) and to use only batch-tested supplements (e.g., Informed-
Sport). 
 
Enforcement and Termination of Membership 
● Right to Investigate: LeisureWorld reserves the right to investigate any suspected breaches of this 
policy to ensure the safety and integrity of the facility environment. 
● Immediate Termination: Any customer found to be using, possessing, or distributing prohibited 
substances or PEDs within or around LeisureWorld premises will have their membership/access 
terminated immediately and permanently. 
● Reporting: In cases involving the illicit distribution or trafficking of prohibited substances, LeisureWorld 
reserves the right to report the matter to Sport Ireland and relevant law enforcement authorities. 
 
Confidential Reporting & Resources 
Customers who have questions regarding this policy, or who wish to report a suspected breach in total 
confidence, should contact the Duty Manager. Further information and verification tools can be accessed 
directly at www.sportireland.ie/anti-doping.

label: LeisureWorld – Safe Selling Supplements & Sport Food Statement
text:
Reviewed June 29 2026 LeisureWorld – Safe Selling Supplements & Sport  Food Statement V1 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Safe Selling Supplements 
& Sport Food Statement 
 
 
At LeisureWorld, the health, safety, and informed choice of our customers are our highest priorities. In accordance with 
our Clean Sport & Anti-Doping Policy and standard-setting bodies like Sport Ireland, Ireland Active, and the Food Safety 
Authority of Ireland (FSAI), we operate a fully compliant and transparent retail environment for sports foods and dietary 
supplements.  
 
This statement applies to all sports nutrition products, sports drinks, and protein bars sold on our premises, including all 
items dispensed via our vending machines. 
 
• Legal Registration & Food Safety Compliance 
o HSE & FSAI Notification: LeisureWorld is fully registered with the local Environmental Health Office 
(EHO) of the Health Service Executive (HSE) as a business selling food supplements and sports food 
products. We have officially notified the Food Safety Authority of Ireland (FSAI) of all relevant products in 
our retail inventory. 
o Traceability & Packaging: All sports foods and food supplements for sale on site are sourced exclusively 
from reputable manufacturers holding ISO 9001 quality standards. They are sold only in their original, 
sealed manufacturer packaging (never decanted or loose). 
o Consumer Rights: In strict adherence to the Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (CCPC) 
policy and the Sale of Goods and Supply of Services Act, 1980, all customer pricing, product information, 
and statutory rights are clearly displayed, accurate, and kept up to date. 
 
• Marketing and Health Claims 
o No Unauthorised Claims: LeisureWorld strictly complies with Regulation (EC) No 1924/2006 on nutrition 
and health claims. 
o We do not promote, display, or tolerate non-authorised health claims. This includes any marketing 
materials or verbal product recommendations from our staff regarding unsubstantiated benefits, 
particularly those relating to rapid weight gain or weight loss. 
 
• Product Screening & Quality Standards (Exceeded & Outstanding) 
o To protect our recreational customers and competitive athletes alike, we screen our product inventory 
against rigorous safety frameworks: 
o The Sport Ireland Checklist: All retail products are verified against the Sport Ireland supplement checklist 
to ensure safety and regulatory compliance. 
o Informed-Sport Batch Testing: Moving beyond standard compliance, we proactively verify our inventory 
against the Informed-Sport List. We focus on sourcing sports foods and supplements that have been 
independently batch-tested to ensure they are free from WADA-prohibited substances, actively 
supporting our members in meeting their personal strict liability obligations.  
 
For more information on our zero-tolerance policy regarding prohibited substances, please consult the LeisureWorld 
Clean Sport & Anti-Doping Policy available on our website or speak to the Duty Manager. Verification tools can be 
accessed directly at www.sportireland.ie/anti-doping.

label: Gender Pay Gap Report 2025
text:
Sport Ionad Réigiúnach Chorcaí CTR. 
T/A LeisureWorld 
Gender Pay Gap Report 2025 
November 2025 
 
 
1. Introduction 
The Gender Pay Gap Information Act 2021 introduced the legislative basis for 
gender pay gap reporting in Ireland and requires organisations to report on their 
hourly gender pay gap. Under recent amendments to legislation, organisations with 
more than 50 employees must now report by selecting a "snapshot" date in June to 
base their reporting. 
 
The snapshot date chosen by the company was the 30th of June 2025. A 
headcount of all employees on this date was conducted, and the gender pay 
information was calculated based on those employees' remuneration between 1st of 
July 2024 and 30th of June 2025. 
 
This report presents the Employment profile and the Gender Pay Gap profile for the 
reporting period. 
 
The company has a mean gender pay gap of 4.14% in favour of men and a median 
pay gap of -18.24% in favour of women.  
 
For part-time employees, the mean gender pay gap is -14.37% in favour of women 
and the median gender pay gap is 50.92% in favour of men. 
 
The report includes an analysis of the reported pay gap and measures being 
undertaken to reduce it.  
 
Appendix 1 contains a summary checklist confirming that all reporting requirements 
have been met. 
 
  
 
 
2. Definitions 
 
• Gender Pay Gap (GPG): The gender pay gap is the difference on average 
across a population between men's and women's pay. The gender pay gap is 
usually represented as the average difference in gross hourly earnings of men 
and of women, expressed as a percentage of men's average gross hourly 
earnings. 
 
o A gender pay gap which is positive indicates that, on average, women 
are in a less favourable position than men. 
o A gender pay gap which is negative indicates the reverse - that, on 
average, men are in a less favourable position than women. 
o It is important to note that the company respects gender as a 
spectrum, to include those who are non-binary, and we are reporting 
as per the legislative requirements. 
 
• Employee Hourly Rate: The hourly remuneration of an employee is 
calculated by dividing the employee’s total ordinary pay according to the 
reporting period by the hours worked for that period. Ordinary pay includes: 
the normal salary paid to the employee; Sunday premium; pay for sick leave; 
any salary top-ups for statutory leaves like maternity / paternity / parent’s 
leave. 
 
• Mean Hourly GPG: The mean gender pay gap is the difference in the 
arithmetic average hourly pay for women compared to men, within our 
organisation. 
 
• Median Hourly GPG: The median gender pay gap is the difference between 
women's median hourly pay (the middle-paid woman) and men's median 
hourly pay (the middle-paid man). The median hourly pay is calculated by 
ranking all employees from the highest paid to the lowest paid and taking the 
hourly pay of the person in the middle. 
 
• Quartiles: Employees were organised into quartiles based on hourly 
remuneration of all male and female full-time employees: lower, lower middle, 
upper middle and upper. The proportion of male and female employees in 
each quartile was expressed as a percentage. 
 
• Snapshot Date: Employers to whom the reporting obligations apply are 
required to calculate and publish the gender pay gap information in respect of 
relevant persons employed by them on the chosen snapshot date, with the 
calculations to be based on those employees' remuneration for the 12-month 
period that precedes the snapshot date. Employers must choose a snapshot 
date. The snapshot date must be in June but may be any date in June. 
 
  
 
3. Data 
 
3.1 Source of Data 
 
The Quantum payroll software used by the company provided pay information 
relevant to the reporting period. 
 
3.2 Data Protection 
 
All processing was conducted in line with Data Protection obligations. All statistics 
provided in this report are combined and do not identify individuals. 
 
 
4. Employment Profile 
 
On 30th of June 2025, there were 89 employees in the company included in the 
report.

6. Analysis 
 
The Gender Pay Gap is the difference in the average hourly wage of men and women across a 
workforce. It is important to distinguish this from Equal Pay.  
The company operates under pay scales decided on by the Board of Directors, 
regardless of gender, ensuring equal pay for equal work. 
 
While the company has equal pay for men and women in the same roles, we have a 
mean gender pay gap of 4.14% in favour of men and a median gender pay gap of 
-18.24% in favour of women. 
 
These results are influenced by the distribution of gender across the grading 
structure: 
• Timing:  
o The gender pay profile is correlated to, and affected by the timing of 
employee joiner, leaver, mobility, and promotion activities. 
• Seniority and Representation:  
o The quartile data highlights a higher representation of men in 
operations management at the snapshot date, which are higher-paid 
roles.  
o In the Upper Middle Quartile (Quartile 3), 55% of employees are male, 
compared to 45% female. 
o Conversely, the Lower Quartile (Quartile 1) has a higher 
representation of women (57%) compared to men (43%). These roles 
are typically reception and cleaning staff roles and have a higher 
percentage of female representation which is in line proportionally with 
the gender of the job applications for these roles.
 
 
• Part-Time Trends:  
o For part -time employees, the gap is significantly positive (50.92% 
median) in favour of women.  
o This indicates that most of the part- time roles are held by men (54%), 
and these men are, on average,  at lower grades or points on the pay 
scale than the smaller number of women (46%) working part-time.  
o This is influenced by the type of work undertaken by these higher paid 
women, e.g., private swim lessons, class instructors. These roles 
currently have a higher percentage of female representation.
 
 
  
 
 
 
7. Measures being taken to eliminate or reduce the Gender Pay Gap 
 
Recruitment & Promotional Practices 
 
The company is committed to ensuring that our workforce reflects the diversity of 
the society we serve. Recruitment is largely fulfilled by advertising jobs publicly , 
with transparent pay ranges, adhering to company policy. 
 
• Interviewer teams are gender balanced. 
• Training is provided to interviewers on equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) 
to mitigate unconscious bias. 
 
Learning & Development 
 
We continue to prioritise Learning and Development to support career progression: 
 
• Mentoring programmes and leadership development courses are available to 
all staff. 
 
Work-Life Balance 
 
To support retention and progression, the company offers: 
 
• Blended working policy, where possible. 
• Flexible working hours (flexitime), where possible. 
• These policies aim to support all employees, particularly those with caring 
responsibilities, to remain in the workforce and progress to senior roles. 
 
 
Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) 
 
LeisureWorld is an Equal Opportunities Employer and does not discriminate on 
grounds of, gender, marital status, family status, sexual orientation, race, religion, 
age, disability, membership of the Traveller community in employment, promotion, 
practices or procedures. 
 
The company’s EDI initiatives focus on promoting an inclusive culture. Our aim is to 
promote a positive inclusive workplace culture where all colleagues feel respected, 
supported and valued.

KIDS CAMPKIDS CAMPINFORMATIONINFORMATION
The camp Drop off time is 9am and collection
is 3pm.
Camp Essentials:
Each day we would ask parents to ensure
children have:
Comfortable shoes / trainers suited for
indoor / outdoor play and sports
Swimwear and a towel, (swim hats are
compulsory in LeisureWorld, goggles are
optional, please also note that we ask that
all kids are able to fully change themselves
for the swimming time)
A packed lunch (Small & Big Lunch)
Bottle of water 
Hat & Sun cream if necessary
Please note there will not be any Vending
machine access throughout the week
KIDS CAMPKIDS CAMPINFORMATIONINFORMATION
Please see below a rough lay out of the day
(subject to change based on external bookings
and weather)
Sample Schedule
9:00 - 9:20 Sign in
9:20 - 9:45 Icebreakers
9:45 - 10:45 Outdoor Activities
10:45 - 11:00 Lunch
11:00 - 12:00 Outdoor games
12:00 - 12:30 Indoor Games
12:30 - 13:00 Lunch
13:00 - 13:45 Talent show
13:45 - 14:45 Swimming 
15:00 Collection
If you have any further queries before the
beginning of the camp, please do not hesitate
to contact us on info@leisureworldcork.com.
